messages:
maya: Heads-up — FedRAMP prep: we need to validate operator entitlements for BYOK imports and run an operator-entitlement scan before the auditor walk on 4/12. Anyone got a short checklist? :spiral_calendar:

liam: I can lead the scan. Quick things to confirm: which roles can call the HSM import API, who has keystore restore/unseal rights, and any Kubernetes service accounts bound to those roles. Also need log evidence for any import/unwrap ops in the past 90 days.

toni: From compliance POV: auditors will want proof of least-privilege, dual-operator for escrow (if applicable), and retention settings for audit logs (90 days min, ideally immutable). We need to show how we assert separation between ops and sec.

maya: Helpful. For scope: this is for Private (customer-managed keys) onboarding path — BYOK imports into our HSM proxy. Not the hosted-only flow.

ops_julio: Ops notes: the HSM proxy only accepts imports when the import feature flag is on; we gate via RBAC group `hsm-import-ops`. Current IAM mapping is GSuite group -> role binding in k8s -> sidecar SA. I can dump bindings.

liam: Please run this locally and paste results (redact emails):
```bash
kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.subjects != null) | {name: .metadata.name, subjects: .subjects}' | grep -A2 hsm
```

ops_julio: pasted output to #sec-tickets and linked ticket SEC-1423. It shows `clusterrolebinding/hsm-import-ops-binding` with subjects: `svcacct:hsm-sidecar:importer-sa` and group `security-operators@redwood.com`

maya: OK — next: audit logging. We need to prove a tamper-evident chain for import events. Current pipeline sends HSM proxy logs into centralized audit with write-once retention in GCS. Toni — do we have immutable retention turned on for customer key events?

toni: We have object hold for the `audit-bucket/keys` prefix enabled for 180 days, and retention policy at 365 days org-wide. For auditors, I can produce export showing object holds for the relevant prefix. Also have log signatures from the HSM proxy (sha256) attached as metadata.

liam: Good. One open question: our KMS integration accepts wrapped keys from customers; do we record the customer proof-of-possession attestation for each import (the HSM requires an attestation blob)? We should show mapping between import request ID and attestation blob ID in logs.

maya: We do capture `import_request_id` and attach `attestation_id` to the event. Ops — can you grep last 30 days for imports and confirm every event has both fields?

ops_julio: quick grep: `grep -E \"import_request_id|attestation_id\" /var/log/hsm-proxy/import.log | wc -l` returns 24 matches; running a quick script to group by request id and check missing attestation.

ops_julio: script output: 24 imports, 24 with attestation metadata, 0 missing. I attached the anonymized audit extract to SEC-1423.

liam: Nice. Now RBAC change: I propose to tighten `hsm-import-ops` so only `security-operators` group can escalate import flags; move `importer-sa` to just namespace-local SA and remove cluster-admin grant. Proposed diff:
```diff
- clusterrolebinding/hsm-import-ops-binding: importer-sa (cluster) + security-operators
+ rolebinding/hsm-import-ops-binding (namespace=hsm): importer-sa (sa) + security-operators
```

toni: From compliance: acceptable as long as you can demonstrate change control (PR history), and a canary period with audit monitoring. Also need to document the rollback plan if import pipeline breaks for a customer.

maya: Agreed. Also need to update runbook: `BYOK-import-incident.md` with steps for emergency key recovery and contact list (Legal, CISO, Customer Success).

liam: I'll open a PR for RBAC change + runbook updates. Can someone volunteer to run a tabletop drill simulating a rogue import? It should exercise incident response and evidence collection.

toni: Compliance will join. Suggest scenario: attacker spins up importer-SA creds, attempts import, we detect via log signature mismatch and block. We'll validate alerts fired in 60s and playbook executed.

ops_julio: I'll coordinate the drill. Plan: create a test tenant, flip feature flag to on in staging, run a simulated import that intentionally provides invalid attestation, verify HSM proxy rejects and raises `SECURITY_IMPORT_ATTTEST_FAIL` metric to SLO dashboard.

security-bot: Created drill task SEC-1423-DRILL and scheduled for 3/31 10:00 PDT. Participants: maya, liam, toni, ops_julio.

maya: Perfect — after drill, we need an artifacts bundle for the auditor: PR diff, RBAC binding snapshot, audit extracts, runbook, and drill postmortem. Toni — can compliance compile templates?

toni: Yes, will assemble artifacts and generate a cover letter describing controls. I might ask for raw logs if auditors want full chain-of-custody.

liam: One more vuln-triage note: we found CVE-2025-XXXX in the HSM proxy dependency chain last week. Patch is staged; making sure RBAC change doesn't interfere with hotfix rollout. Ops — ensure hotfix plan includes steps to re-run import tests after patch.

ops_julio: Hotfix window scheduled 3/28 02:00-03:00 UTC in staging, 4/2 in prod with rollback. Will include import smoke tests in both windows.

maya: Thanks everyone. Action items: liam -> PR for RBAC + tests; ops_julio -> exports + run drill; toni -> artifacts + cover letter; maya -> coordinate auditor package. We'll post progress in SEC-1423. :thumbsup:
